result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.cmty_label_propagation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Detect communities by asynchronous label propagation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L26027-L26115){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.cmty_label_propagation( seed=None, max_iter=100, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Label propagation communities](/assets/graphs/cmty-label-propagation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two dense clusters, a triangle A, B, C and a four-node cluster D, E, F, G, joined by the single edge C to D. Starting from one label per node, each node repeatedly adopts its neighbors' most common label; the labels settle on the two clusters, drawn in the accent color and teal. The card lists community 0 as A, B, C and community 1 as D, E, F, G." width="100%"} Every node starts with a label of its own. Nodes are then visited in random order, and each adopts the label carried by the most edges (or the most edge weight, on a weighted graph) among its neighbors, breaking ties at random. Labels spread through densely connected regions and stall at sparse boundaries; when a full pass changes nothing, each remaining label is a community (Raghavan, Albert & Kumara, 2007). Label propagation needs no parameters and runs in near-linear time, so it scales to very large graphs. It does not optimize any objective, and different seeds can give different partitions, so it is best for a fast first look; use `cmty_leiden()` when partition quality matters. Edge direction is ignored. This is the unsupervised community detection method that NetworkX calls `asyn_lpa_communities()`. It is different from `label_propagation()`, which spreads a few *known* labels to classify the remaining nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the visiting order and tie-breaking. Set it for reproducible results. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of passes over the nodes. Label propagation almost always settles much sooner; the cap guards against rare oscillations. Default is `100`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store community labels in. If `None` (default), uses `"cmty_label_propagation"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the community labels as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, int], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to community labels (`0`, `1`, ..., numbered in order of the lowest node ID in each). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two cliques joined by a single edge each settle on one label: ::: {#3133126d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("E", "H"), ("F", "G"), ("F", "H"), ("G", "H"), ("D", "E")]) ) communities = graph.cmty_label_propagation(seed=3, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(n): c for n, c in sorted(communities.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 0, 'B': 0, 'C': 0, 'D': 0, 'E': 1, 'F': 1, 'G': 1, 'H': 1} ``` ::: :::
